stage_2_story.text_en:
Avi decided it was time to repaint the living room. The old paint had faded and there were a few cracks in the wall. He planned to do the work over the weekend.

On Saturday morning, he moved the furniture to the center of the room and spread a large drop cloth over everything. Then he stuck masking tape carefully along the baseboards, window frames, and ceiling edges so the paint would not go where it was not supposed to.

He opened the paint can and used a stirrer to mix the paint until it was smooth. Before painting the walls, he took a piece of sandpaper and rubbed the cracks and rough spots until the surface was even. Then he rolled primer onto the entire wall and let it dry for an hour.

When the primer was dry, Avi poured the light grey paint into the paint tray and loaded the roller. He painted the large flat areas of the wall with the roller in long smooth strokes. For the corners and edges, he switched to a smaller paintbrush.

After the first layer dried, the color looked a little thin and uneven in some places. So Avi applied a second coat, starting from the top and working down. This time the color looked rich and even.

Miriam came in to check the progress. She looked at the walls and smiled. "It looks like a different room," she said. Avi peeled off the masking tape carefully, folded up the drop cloth, and cleaned his roller and paintbrush in the sink. The living room looked fresh and new.
